CTR Reload 0.7.5 Beta is a native Windows version of Crash Team Racing (PS1, 1999) that loads custom tracks and custom characters. It contains no game data: you need your own NTSC-U disc image (SCUS-94426, .cue/.bin). Download ctr_native.exe and ReloadStudio.exe into one folder you can write to; the game asks for the disc image on the first start. README.txt explains the rest.

For custom characters with animations this release also carries a Blender template, driver-template.blend (free for any use, CC0 - see LICENSE-template.txt), and the guide ANIMATIONS.txt. SHA256SUMS.txt lists the checksums of these three files.

Versioning reset: 0.7.5 follows 0.0.5. From now on versions count 0.x.y in steps of 0.0.5 (0.7.5, 0.8.0, 0.8.5 ...).

New in 0.7.5
- Custom characters can bring their own ground shadow and exhaust: a shadow fitted to the model's footprint (or none), and the exhaust at one or two points of the model (or none). The exhaust smoke and the turbo flames follow these points. Characters built before keep the original shadow, smoke and flames.
- Reload Studio: glTF binary (.glb) is now the recommended model format. The file dialog lists "glTF binary (*.glb) - recommended" first. One .glb brings everything at once: all meshes of the scene (as one driver), UVs, normals, materials and the textures inside the file; a .gltf finds its textures next to it. Reload Studio reads it like an OBJ, with the same rules, limits and messages, and a .glb dropped onto the page is the model. OBJ and PLY stay as they are for models without animations.
- Reload Studio: every card of the Character page is open without a start switch - Native model, In the race, Wheels and Animations. "Coming soon" is left only on the page Track, for Time Trial and Battle, the modes that are not built yet.
- Reload Studio: the Character page fits smaller screens without scrolling (for example 1366 x 768 at 150 %).
- Reload Studio, Character page: a new 3D preview. Drag to turn the model and to look from higher or lower, drag with the right or middle mouse button to move it, turn the mouse wheel to zoom to the point under the pointer, double-click to reset. Fixed views Front, Side, Back, Top, 3/4 and Race (the in-game chase camera) are on a bar in the preview and in its View menu (also on a right-click), with the shadow and the exhaust (shown or hidden), the Crash size reference (on or off) and a dark or light background. These switches only change what you see, never the character file.
- Reload Studio: a file named portable.ini next to ReloadStudio.exe (it may be empty) keeps its settings, logs and temporary files in that folder instead of %APPDATA% and %TEMP%, as the switch --settings does; the packer that Reload Studio runs keeps its temporary files there as well.
- Fix: in an arcade cup the custom driver is no longer dropped at the podium.
- Fix: an OBJ material with a texture and an emission colour (Ke) but no diffuse colour is no longer drawn darker. Characters built from such a model get other colours when you build them again.

Animations for custom characters
- A custom character can bring its own poses. Make them as shape keys on the driver mesh in Blender and export the model as a .glb; the base mesh is the neutral pose, and each key is the full pose. Seven names, all optional (upper or lower case does not matter):
  - steer_left and steer_right: the lean at full lock to the driver's left or right. The driver blends into it along the steering curve of the original drivers. With only one of the two, the other side is its mirror image when the model is symmetric; if it is not, both sides keep the automatic lean and Reload Studio says "model not symmetric, using automatic lean".
  - reverse: driving backwards.
  - crash: the hit and the bounce after a crash, at its strongest point.
  - jump: in the air.
  - win and lose: after the finish line of a race with a real placing (not in a time trial), win for places 1-3 and lose for places 4-8. The driver blends into the pose in about half a second.
- A pose without its shape key is filled in automatically: steering, reverse, crash and jump move as before, win and lose stay neutral. A key that is exported but empty keeps that pose still. Shape keys with other names are ignored and listed. The kart stays still in every pose.
- Steering, reverse, crash and jump are built into every animation frame of the character, so the game shows them with NATIVE DRIVERS on or off. Win and lose show only on the high-detail model: they are built only with "Native model" ticked in Reload Studio, and the game shows them with NATIVE DRIVERS set to PREVIEW (see below), after the finish line. The classic model stays neutral after the finish line.
- Rigs (armatures) are not supported yet: a .glb with a rig is refused with "Rigs are not supported yet, please use shape keys".
- Reload Studio, card Animations (tab Extras): open to everyone, no longer "Coming soon". It lists the seven poses and where each comes from: from the file, mirrored, automatic, neutral, or an error with its reason. Without "Native model" win and lose are not built: the list says "used only with the native model" and Win and Lose are greyed out. Its preview plays them: a Steering slider from left to right, Jump, Crash, Reverse, Win and Lose, and Play (loop); a click on a pose in the list shows it. Win and lose play on the Native look; the Classic look stays neutral, as in the game. Nothing of it is built or remembered.
- A driver template for Blender, free for any use (CC0): download driver-template.blend from this release (made with Blender 5.2; older versions may not open it). It is a simple placeholder driver with kart at the right size and orientation, with all seven shape keys and the export settings stored in the file. The guide ANIMATIONS.txt, also on this page, explains the whole way, from the model to the shape keys and the export. The source code carries the guide as docs/ANIMATIONS.md and the script that makes the template (templates/make_driver_template.py); Blender 5.2.2 makes the same file from it.

Preview: high-detail custom characters
- A custom character can carry a second, high-detail model with its real textures, drawn by a new native render path: up to 20,000 vertices, 30,000 triangles and 16 textures (up to 2048 x 2048), sharp at every resolution, also in water, in mud and in the mirror on ice, and in the driver select. Eight different drivers of 30,000 triangles each in one race run smoothly.
- The high-detail model is drawn with the kart wheels hidden ("Show kart wheels" off) or with wheels of its own (see below). A model that shows the kart wheels and has no wheel model keeps its classic model and the game's own wheels.
- Switch it on in the game: OPTIONS -> GRAPHICS -> NATIVE DRIVERS, OFF or PREVIEW (OFF by default). The choice is saved and applies at the next start; until then the page says "NATIVE DRIVERS: AFTER RESTART". The high-detail model is drawn from a resolution of 2x; at 1x, and for every other driver, the game draws as before. For tests, `ctr_native.exe --dev --native-preview` still switches it on for one run.
- By default nothing changes: every file also holds the classic model, and that is what the game draws with NATIVE DRIVERS off.
- Wheels of their own: a character with a high-detail model can bring one wheel model for all four wheels - a .glb, an OBJ (with its MTL file and one texture of up to 1024 x 1024) or a PLY, up to 1024 triangles. The right wheels are its mirror image, the front wheels steer, all four roll with the speed, and the wheel size (50 to 200 %) keeps the bottom of the wheel on the ground. Where the high-detail model is not drawn (NATIVE DRIVERS off, resolution 1x, an older version), the character drives its classic model with the game's own wheels.
- Wheels of their own, complete: a second wheel model for the two rear wheels (for example a wider one; it keeps its size next to the front wheel), each axle moved forward or back and up or down, with its track wider or narrower. Wheels of their own are drawn at every distance.
- At speed the tread of a wheel of its own no longer seems to stand still or to turn backwards. When Reload Studio builds the character, it counts the lugs of each wheel's tread from its shape (4 to 32 lugs, all alike, with a groove between each two) and stores the number when it is certain, so the game can keep the drawn spin well under half a lug per frame (0.30). A smooth wheel, or one whose tread cannot be counted for certain, gets a safe limit that works for any tread of up to 32 lugs: such a wheel never turns backwards, but may look slower than the kart at top speed. The number is stored only when every modelled part of the wheel repeats exactly that often: lugs, groove floors, and also spokes or bolts on the rim. 8 spokes on a 4-lug tyre, or 12 spokes on 10 lugs, mean no count is stored, and the wheel gets the safe limit. A pattern that is only painted on (stripes, painted spokes) is not counted and can still flicker, so model spokes and lugs as real geometry, in step with each other.
- The native render path was measured with eight custom drivers on screen, and the pipelines a race needs are now built while the race loads, so the first frame of the race no longer stalls.
- The Reload Studio preview shows the high-detail model the way the game draws it with NATIVE DRIVERS set to PREVIEW: the real textures in full size, with the same mipmaps as the game. Its View menu switches between Native and Classic (the model the game draws with NATIVE DRIVERS off, with the game's own wheels). A line below the preview says which look you see and names texture files that were not found; such a material is drawn in its colour.
- Reload Studio builds the high-detail model without a start switch: tick "Native model" (tab Extras, card Import, marked "Preview feature"); it needs "Show kart wheels" off or a wheel model. The card Wheels takes the wheel model and its size and shows the wheels in place, steering and spinning, in the preview, also without a body model. It reads the wheel again when you export it again, says why it warns (for example a texture not found) and finds the wheel texture in the Textures folder as well. While the card Wheels is shown, a model dropped onto the page becomes the wheel model; the body keeps its file. Without the tick, Reload Studio builds the same file as before.
- The card Wheels also takes a "Rear wheel model (GLB/OBJ/PLY)" and the axles (Front axle or Rear axle, with Fwd, Up and Track). The preview shows the rear wheel and the moved axles at once. Each of these goes into the file only when you set it; left alone, the character is built exactly as before.

Known issues
- Custom drivers without their own voice lines are silent.
- The cup podium shows the template, Fake Crash, in place of the custom driver, so win and lose are not seen there.
- Win and lose show only on the high-detail model (built with "Native model", NATIVE DRIVERS set to PREVIEW, resolution 2x or more). At the finish line the driver first jumps a little from its steering pose, then blends into win or lose.
- Rigs are not supported yet: animations come only from shape keys.
- Wheels of their own: when the lugs cannot be counted for certain from the shape of the wheel (a smooth wheel, lugs that are not all alike, spokes or bolts that do not repeat as often as the lugs, or a tread painted only in the texture), the wheel seems to turn slower than the kart drives at top speed. A painted pattern with more repeats than the stored count, or than 32, may still flicker at speed.
- Drivers exported with earlier builds should be re-exported in Reload Studio to get correct wheel tread animation.
- Native drivers in split-screen are not performance-optimized yet.
- Custom tracks: Battle is not built yet, and Time Trial has no entry of its own ("Coming soon"); the time trial is under RACE, MODE.

Good to know
- Characters go into the characters folder next to the game, tracks into tracks. The game reads both folders when it starts: after a new driver or track, restart the game.
- NATIVE DRIVERS is off by default: without it the game draws every custom character with its classic model, as before.
- The format of the high-detail model is a preview and may still change; a later version may ask you to build such a character again.
- Wheels of their own need this version: an older version refuses that part of the file and drives the character's classic model with the game's own wheels.
- Animations and older versions: a character without shape keys, and every OBJ or PLY, is built exactly as before. Steering, reverse, crash and jump from shape keys are part of the classic model, so every version shows them. An older version ignores win and lose. A file with a rear wheel model, moved axles or a stored tread count needs this version: an older version draws its classic model with the game's own wheels.
- This is a beta: expect rough edges. Report bugs as GitHub issues: https://github.com/LinksTech/CTR-Reload-Edition/issues
